author: Sawan Mukhiya
text:
From May 6 to July 6, 2026, I had the opportunity to work as an AI/ML Engineering Intern at Camden Tools Ltd — and what a two months it has been 🎉

Working on a real, production-grade system from day one was humbling and exhilarating in equal measure. My core contribution was building a compliance-aware product classification pipeline — spanning four restricted inventory categories — that went all the way from raw, messy data to a live, decision-making system serving an actual business workflow.

Along the way, I got deep hands-on experience with things I once only read and prototyped about:
- Training and tuning XGBoost & LightGBM models with Optuna and grounding them in 384-dim SentenceTransformer embeddings — achieving F1 scores of 0.95, 0.97, 0.96, and 0.94 across the four classification domains (knives, fragile goods, liquids, and electrical plugs)
- Designing a FastAPI microservice with a three-zone probability decision system — items scoring within a calibrated uncertainty band around the threshold are flagged for human review, while high- and low-confidence predictions are auto-labeled — keeping reviewers focused only where the model genuinely wasn't sure
- Building a real-time Next.js Admin Dashboard wired into the ML backend — so reviewers could audit, resolve, and override model decisions with full auditability
- Dockerizing the entire ML + API stack for scalable production deployment

What I didn't expect was how much I'd grow in "thinking like an engineer" — balancing model performance with operational reliability, and learning that a great ML model is only as good as the system it lives inside.

I'm deeply grateful to the team at Camden Tools, Shreejal Maharjan for trusting me with real problems, real data, and real stakes. This experience has made me more certain than ever that my path lies in building intelligent, production-ready AI systems.

If you're working on ML infrastructure, AI-powered workflows, or just want to chat about the intersection of models and software engineering — I'd love to connect! 🤝
